title: PU-05-047 — Order on Consent Agreement Order
text:
221 PU-05-47 Filed 06/29/2022 Pages: 9
Order on Consent Agreement
Public Service Commission

Administrative Code section 69-06-11-02 for the installation of a functioning light-
mitigating technology system at the Rugby Wind Farm.

On November 17, 2021, the Commission issued a notice for public hearing on the
second application for extension in the above captioned case.

On December 17, 2021, the Commission held a public hearing as noticed.

On December 29, 2021, the Commission denied Rugby’s second request for an
extension to install ADLS.

On January 5, 2022, Staff sent Rugby a Notice of Noncompliance, noting that
Rugby had violated N.D.C.C. 49-22-16.4(3) and N.D.A.C. 69-06-11-02(2) by failing to
have a functioning ADLS at the Rugby Wind Farm by December 31, 2021. The Notice of
Noncompliance noted that Rugby may be subject to civil penalty pursuant to N.D.C.C.
49-22-21 and that, in addition, the Commission may suspend or revoke the Certificate of
Site Compatibility issued for Rugby for operation in violation of N.D.C.C., N.D.A.C., or
provisions of the Commission’s Order issuing the Certificate.

On February 10, 2022, Commission staff sent a request to Rugby for status
updates on the installation progress of its ADLS.

On March 4, 2022, Commission staff received an update from Rugby, stating other
civil work had been undertaken and completed while waiting for components to arrive.
The tower had been erected and the remaining components were received and installed
and testing of the ADLS Radar system was beginning.

On March 28, 2022, a second monthly status stated that on March 18, 2022, the
ADLS system became operational.

Discussion

Rugby Wind owns and operates the Rugby Wind farm. Rugby Wind Farm is a
150-megawatt wind farm located in Pierce County.

North Dakota Century Code ("N.D.C.C.") Section 49-22-16.4(3) requires that "by
December 31, 2021, every wind energy conversion facility for which the commission
issued a certificate of site compatibility before June 5, 2016, must be equipped with a
functioning light-mitigating technology system that complies with rules adopted by the
commission. After a public hearing, the commission may grant a waiver or an extension
of time based on technical or economic feasibility considerations." See also North Dakota
Administrative Code ("N.D.A.C.") Section 69-06-11-02(1).

Certificate of Site Compatibility No. 5 for the Rugby Wind Farm was issued before
June 5, 2016; therefore, it was required by N.D.C.C. Section 49-22-16.4(3) and N.D.A.C.

Case No. PU-05-47

Page 2 of 3

Section 69-06-11-02(2) to be equipped with a functioning light-mitigating technology by
December 31, 2021. Commission Staff investigated the matter and concluded that Rugby
Wind violated N.D.C.C. Section 49-22-16.4(3) and N.D.A.C. Section 69-06-11-02(2) by
failing to have a functioning light mitigation technology at the Rugby Wind Farm by
December 31, 2021.

Rugby Wind and Advocacy Staff engaged in good faith settlement discussions
resulting in a Consent Agreement intended to avoid further administrative proceedings or
litigation.

Under the Consent Agreement, Rugby Wind and Advocacy Staff compromised to
a penalty of $24,000 due to outside forces and supply chain issues.

Having considered this matter, the Commission finds the Consent Agreement filed
on June 2, 2022, is reasonable and acceptable. Therefore, the Commission issues the
following:

Order

The Commission Orders:

1. The Consent Agreement between Rugby and Advocacy Staff filed with the
Commission on June 2, 2022, is approved. A copy of the Consent Agreement is
attached to and made a part of this Order on Consent Agreement (Order).

2. Rugby is assessed a civil penalty of $24,000 for violating N.D.C.C. Section 49-
22-16.4(3) and N.D.A.C. Section 69-06-11-02(2), and PPM agrees to remit the $24,000
payable to the North Dakota Public Service Commission within ten business days of
service of an Order accepting or approving the Consent Agreement.

c. Violates any provision of this chapter or any rule adopted by the commission
pursuant to this chapter.”

Certificate of Site Compatibility - Energy Conversion Facility
On October 3, 2005, in Case No. PU-05-47, the North Dakota Public Utility
Commission (Commission) issued Certificate of Site Compatibility Number 5 to Rugby’s
predecessor, PPM Energy, Inc., designating a site for the construction, operation and
maintenance of an energy conversion facility site for the Rugby Wind Farm _ in Pierce
County, North Dakota. On December 3, 2008, in Case No. PU-05-47, the Commission
reissued Certificate of Site Compatibility Number 5 to Rugby Wind, LLC to construct and

operate the Rugby Wind Farm in Pierce County, North Dakota.

ADLS Installation at Rugby Wind Farm
On March 22, 2021, Rugby Wind, LLC filed with the Commission a request for extension,
from December 31, 2021, to December 31, 2022. Rugby Wind requested that the
Commission consider and issue a decision on the extension as soon as is possible,
stating “if an extension is not granted by May, 2021, Rugby will be required to procure the
ADLS system.”

On April 20, 2021, an informal hearing was held on the request for extension.

On May 10, 2021, Commission Staff filed a Memorandum supplementing the
record regarding the approval status of Light Intensity Dimming Solution (LIDS)
technology by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA).

On May 27, 2021, Rugby sent a letter informing the Commission that it would no

longer pursue the LIDS technology, stating “[a]t this time, we are expediting the ADLS

2

light mitigation solution in order to meet the existing statutory deadline of December 31,
2021.”

On June 9, 2021, the Commission denied the first extension request.

On November 2, 2021, PPM filed a second extension request, based upon
unanticipated supply chain issues, to extend the deadline from December 31, 2021, to
May 31, 2022, under North Dakota Century Code section 49-22-16.4 and North Dakota
Administrative Code section 69-06-11-02 for the installation of a functioning light-
mitigating technology system at the Rugby Wind Farm.

On November 17, 2021, the Commission issued a notice for public hearing on the
second application for extension in the above captioned case.

On December 17, 2021, the Commission held a public hearing as noticed.

On December 29, 2021, the Commission denied Rugby’s second request for an
extension to install ADLS.

On January 5, 2022, Staff sent Rugby a Notice of Noncompliance, noting that NSP
had violated N.D.C.C. 49-22-16.4(3) and N.D.A.C. 69-06-11-02(2) by failing to have a
functioning ADLS at Rugby Wind Farm by December 31, 2021. The Notice of
Noncompliance noted that Rugby may be subject to civil penalty pursuant to N.D.C.C.
49-22-21, and that, in addition, the Commission may suspend or revoke the Certificate of
Site Compatibility issued for Rugby for operation in violation of N.D.C.C., N.D.A.C., or
provisions of the Commission’s Order issuing the Certificate.

On February 10, 2022 Commission staff sent a request to Rugby Wind LLC for

status updates on the installation progress on its ADLS installation.

On March 4, 2022, Commission staff received an update from Rugby Wind LLC,
stating other civil work had been undertaken and completed while waiting for components
to arrive. The tower had been erected and the remaining components were received and
installed and testing of the ADLS Radar system was beginning.

On March 28, 2022, a second monthly status stating that on March 18, 2022 the
ADLS system became operational.

Terms of Consent Agreement

Rugby and Staff engaged in good faith settlement discussions regarding this
Matter resulting in this Consent Agreement. Having agreed that settlement of this Matter
will avoid further administrative proceedings or litigation and that entry of this Consent
Agreement is the most appropriate means of resolving this Matter, the Staff and Rugby
agree on the following terms, subject to the approval and acceptance of the Commission:

1. Staff and Rugby agree to settle the Matter on the following terms:

a. Rugby acknowledges that it did not have a functioning ADLS by December
31, 2021, and therefore did not comply with N.D.C C. 49-22-16.4(3) and
N DAC. 69-06-11-02(2).

b. Subject to the provisions of this Agreement, Rugby agrees to a civil penalty,
payable to the North Dakota Public Service Commission, of $48,000 for not
complying with the ADLS statute.

c. As provided in N.D.C.C. 49-22-21(3) the civil penalty may be compromised
by the Commission. The Commission acknowledges outside forces and
events due to supply chain issues and the Covid pandemic that contributed
to the delayed implementation of Rugby Winds ADLS system and reduces

the civil Penalty to $24,000.

2. There are no covenants, promises, undertakings, or understandings related to the
resolution of the Matter other than those specifically set forth in this Agreement
and Order.

3. This agreement may be executed in counterparts and duplicate copies, each which
shall be deemed to be an original, and which, when taken together, shall constitute
one and the same instrument.

4. The undersigned on behalf of Rugby is authorized to act on behalf of Rugby and
bind Rugby for purposes of this Consent Agreement and knows and fully

understands the content and effect of this Consent Agreement.
